title: Sulfur signaling: from molecules to physiological responses
content: Sulfur metabolism plays a central role in determining plant resilience in environments where nutrient availability fluctuates and plants are exposed to both biotic and abiotic stressors. As an essential macronutrient, sulfur is vital for the structural and catalytic integrity of proteins, cofactors, and metabolites that enable plants to withstand drought, salinity, pathogen attack, and oxidative stress. Unlike other mineral nutrients, sulfur is incorporated into a uniquely diverse set of bioactive molecules whose functions extend far beyond features attributed to the primary metabolites. This biochemical versatility makes sulfur not only indispensable for growth but also a key component of the adaptive capacity of plants in the face of dynamic environmental challenges.
